text:
maria: Heads-up: midnight perf alert triggered on the sampler/payload-coalescer path after today's merge. p95 latency +45%, throughput roughly flat. :eyes:
aj: https://dash.redwood.ai/alerts/ev123 - alert fired at 02:03 UTC, spike looks concentrated on the coalescer hotpath
ci-bot: nightly-perf: job 'sampler-e2e' failed (2026-03-17T02:00Z). baseline p95 420ms -> 610ms. attaching small log excerpt:
```
[02:02:58] sampler: process_request id=abc123 seq=4
[02:02:58] payload_coalescer.cpp:237 flush_if_needed() took 120ms (hot)
[02:02:58] sampler: response served 610ms
```
devon: grabbing a perf flame for the canary runs now, will post samples in a minute
lina: did we change the coalescer thresholds in the last few merges? I remember a PR for batching heuristics yesterday
aj: yes PR #4723 (author noah) adjusted coalescer flush threshold to prefer throughput for long sequences — might be hurting short-seq latency patterns
noah: I can confirm, my change was to increase the flush delay to reduce small write churn for big-batch customers. didn't expect regressions for 1-4 token bursts
devon: local flame shows CPU spent in payload_coalescer::flush_if_needed and a spin-wait path when bursts < 8 tokens. stack sample: payload_coalescer::flush_if_needed -> spin_wait::yield -> kernel_selector::probe
maria: hold the rollout on the merge that added #4723. tagging SRE and will open incident if bisect confirms. @sre oncall please advise
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-0317 created. Priority: P2. Links: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-0317
aj: quick mitigation plan: revert the threshold bump or add an adaptive short-seq override. i'll try a canary with the old threshold value (2ms) on canary cluster right now
devon: starting git bisect over the last 8 merges with a perf smoke. range: 7f3a1b2..main. will run the bisect job via CI
ci-bot: bisect job queued: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/bisect/5143219876. will report first bad/first good commits when done
lina: if bisect hits #4723, recommend emergency revert + a targeted perf test (small-burst workload) in CI to prevent regression slipping back in
noah: i'm standing by to revert/adjust. i also have a variant to make delay adaptive by recent-request-size that might avoid a hard revert
devon: canary telemetry: after setting threshold back to 2ms on canary, p95 returned to baseline (~430ms). looks promising. pushing hotfix branch with threshold knob and test vectors
maria: thanks. please open PR against hotfix and include the small-burst synthetic test and perf guard (fail CI if p95 regresses >10%)
aj: PR created: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4876 - includes knob, tests, and brief notes
devon: re-running nightly perf job against hotfix branch; if green we'll merge and roll-forward with canary monitoring
ci-bot: nightly-perf for hotfix branch finished: baseline p95 425ms -> 435ms (within tolerance). no alert fired
maria: merging hotfix and unblocking rollout. we'll keep the canary ramp slow and watch the dashboards overnight. great triage team work. :tada:
noah: sorry for the regression, thanks for the quick bisect + fix. I'll follow up with a small-seq workload in perf suite
lina: follow-up action: add small-burst test to pre-merge perf check and consider adaptive coalescer heuristic (Lina + Noah + Devon)
maria: closing thread for now. if any oscillation appears overnight, re-open here or escalate to INC-2026-0317.
